summary: Teardown routine for an object holding two linked lists. Flushes a global string buffer, then walks and frees every node of the first list (this+28): each active node's data block is default-initialized, its sub-allocations and the block itself freed, then the node freed. The second list (this+48) is walked and freed the same way. All list bookkeeping fields are zeroed on exit.

operations.description: Call StringCopyWithBufferRealloc(&byte_5EA438) three times to flush/reset the global string buffer.
Zero the first-list count/state byte at this+24.
Walk the first list from head this+28: for each node read the active flag at node+8 and the next pointer at node+4; stop when the next pointer is null.
If the first-list node is active (node+8 flag), take its data block at node+0 and, when non-null, reinitialize it via SessionConfigDefaultInit.
Free the data block's owned sub-allocations (offset 0x14, offset 0x8, and the leading pointer) and then the data block itself with FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Free the first-list node itself with FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Zero the first-list bookkeeping: head this+28, this+32, this+36, this+40 and the flags byte this+44.
Walk the second list from head this+48: for each node read the active flag at node+8 and the next pointer at node+4; when the next pointer is null the loop ends.
If the second-list node is active, free its data block (node+0) with FreeWrapper_7bcf, then free the node itself.
Zero the second-list bookkeeping: head this+48, this+52, this+56 and this+60.
